findings.title: enableSqlExpressions contains dead, inverted feature-flag logic
findings.body: The new `enableSqlExpressions` function computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (note the negation) and then discards the result, returning `false` on both paths. The intent — SQL expressions are hard-disabled due to CVE-2024-9264 — is fine, but the leftover inverted computation is a trap: anyone later 're-enabling' the feature by changing the final `return false` to `return enabled` would invert the flag semantics, enabling SQL expressions when the flag is off and disabling them when it is on. The function should either be `return false` with a comment referencing the CVE, or correct flag logic with the feature removed.

findings.title: Error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' is misleading
findings.body: When a user submits a SQL expression, `ReadQuery` now returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`. The feature is in fact implemented but deliberately disabled for security reasons (CVE-2024-9264 RCE/LFI via DuckDB), including for users who have explicitly enabled the `sqlExpressions` feature flag. The 'not implemented' wording is wrong and gives operators no indication that the feature was disabled on purpose or where to learn why; the message should state that SQL expressions are disabled (ideally referencing the security advisory).

findings.title: Inert stub DB leaves reachable dead code with SQL string interpolation
findings.body: The new stub `DB` makes every method return 'not implemented', which disables the feature, but all the surrounding machinery is kept: `TablesList` in pkg/expr/sql/parser.go still builds a command via `fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)` with hand-rolled quote escaping before calling the stub, and `SQLCommand.Execute` still calls `QueryFramesInto`. Today this is inert only because the stub never executes anything; the dangerous interpolation path remains in the codebase where a future partial revert (e.g., swapping in a real DB implementation 'just for parsing') would silently re-expose it. Consider deleting the parser/command code along with the DuckDB dependency rather than leaving it behind an error stub.
